messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1702501234 — prefix-cache correctness alerts: elevated mismatch rate for prefix 'u:profiles:' across region-us-west. paging eng-oncall @alex and eng-sre @marta. please ack and post status.

alex: acked. seeing a 12% error delta on reads that hit prefix cache, not on direct KV reads.
marta: checking dashboards — prefix hit-rate tanked on some hosts, but KV p99 latency is fine. could be staleness/correctness guard tripping.
samir: adding logs — I'm seeing a repeated reader fallback where the cache returns old entries and the correctness validation layer forces KV bypass. spike in bypass traffic causing downstream pressure.
jess: any customer-facing impact? CS reports elevated 500s for long-running inference jobs in a handful of tenants.
evan: flagged for high-value customers on Dedicated — need mitigation ASAP, but minimize customer-visible changes.
ops-bot: deploy bot: rolling restart triggered on prefix-cache service in region-us-west by alex — build/sha: d4823f.
alex: live plan: 1) throttle prefix-cache acceptance for writes (reduce TTL acceptance) 2) force KV-read fallback for suspicious prefixes to guarantee correctness 3) shape traffic to avoid overloading shard hosts. doing step 1 now.
marta: confirm command?
alex: running: 
```bash
$ infractl config set prefix_cache.write_accept_rate "0.5" --region us-west
# reduces how many writes get accepted into prefix cache; rest go direct to KV
```
marta: applied. watch hit-rate and write queue.
(2 minutes later)
samir: write_accept_rate change acknowledged by all cache nodes. acceptance dropped from ~95% to ~48%. bypass rate increased accordingly. kernel-pool CPU on some frontends jumped 15%.
jess: CS: three customers reported timeouts 12:15-12:20, ticket numbers: CS-989, CS-990, CS-991. triaging.
evan: can we do more surgical routing? disable prefix caching only for offending tenant prefixes instead of global change?
alex: yes, plan B — enable prefix shielding for tenant list. creating patch list for impacted prefixes and will route them to correctness-safe path.
samir: patch command (dry-run):
```yaml
routing:
  prefix_shield:
    - prefix: "u:profiles:tenant-42:"
      mode: bypass
    - prefix: "u:profiles:tenant-77:"
      mode: bypass
```
apply with: `infractl route apply --file shield.yml --region us-west`
marta: please include tenant owners in the shield list.
alex: applied shield for tenant-42 and tenant-77. infractl returned 200.
ops-bot: routing-change: shield applied to 2 prefixes by alex at 1702501450.
samir: after shields, observed per-tenant fallback when those prefixes are requested, overall KV RPS increased on a small subset of nodes but within headroom.
jess: CS updated customers for tenant-42 and -77 with note: "We routed your traffic to a correctness-safe path to prevent stale cache results; you may see slightly higher latency for a short window." :white_check_mark:
evan: good. what about global customers still seeing issues?
alex: still ~5% elevated error delta across unrelated prefixes. hypothesis: a lease/eviction mismatch causing incorrect entries to be served occasionally. mitigation C: enable safety-mode on prefix-cache which enforces stronger validation at cost of latency.
marta: what's command to enable safety-mode?
samir: `infractl feature toggle prefix_cache.safety_mode true --region us-west` — will run a rolling enable to avoid thundering herd.
alex: enabling safety-mode now (rolling over 10% of nodes every 30s).
(approx 6 minutes pass)
samir: safety-mode enabled on 60% nodes; mismatch rate dropped to ~1.8% and error delta trending down. latency p50 increased ~20ms, p95 +120ms on safety-mode hosts.
jess: CS: new customer reports dropped from 3 to 0 in the last 10m. good.
evan: acceptable tradeoff for correctness; let's keep safety-mode until we have root cause.
marta: agree. starting deeper investigation: collecting cache eviction logs, lease/grace periods, and write-ordering traces. I'll capture a 5m trace.
alex: also going to temporarily reduce client-facing concurrency for inference jobs from 8 to 4 for affected tenants to reduce tail latencies while safety-mode is on. command: `infractl quota set tenant-42 concurrency 4`
ops-bot: quota-change: tenant-42 concurrency -> 4 by alex at 1702501820.
samir: note — KV backend saw a small spike in RPS after shields and throttles, auto-scaling handled it. keep an eye on KV throttles.
marta: digging through traces: found race where cache eviction race + delayed invalidation messages can produce a time-window where stale entry is considered valid. root cause likely message reorder in our invalidation pipeline under overload.
ealex: (typo correction) alex: noted. do we have a fast fix?
samir: short-term fix: change invalidation to include monotonic sequence numbers per prefix so nodes can ignore out-of-order invalidations. rolling patch ready, needs canary.
alex: canary plan: rollout sequence-id invalidation to 10% nodes in us-west, monitor mismatch and latency. if safe, ramp to 100% over 30 minutes.
marta: create canary ticket and runbook steps. main mitigation (safety-mode + targeted shields) stays active during rollout.
jess: CS: prepping customer comms with ETA for full restoration.
evan: schedule a postmortem call tomorrow 16:00 PT. assign owners.
(30 minutes later)
ops-bot: deploy bot: canary of seq-invalidation rolled to 10% nodes by samir at 1702503200.
samir: canary looks clean after 8 mins — mismatch rate on canary nodes 0.1% vs 1.8% elsewhere. starting slow ramp to 40%.
marta: continuing tracing; collecting sample invalidation ordering logs to compare.
alex: handoff: I'm going offline in 45m. @marta you'll be the primary oncall after 18:00 PT. leaving notes in the incident doc with commands and current config.
marta: got it. please include list of tenants shielded and actions taken.
alex: included. quick summary pushed to /incidents/1702501234/doc: safety-mode=on, shielded-prefixes=["u:profiles:tenant-42:","u:profiles:tenant-77:"], write_accept_rate=0.5, quota-reductions applied, seq-invalidation canary in progress.
(closure)
marta: seq-invalidation ramp completed to 100% at 1702503600. mismatch rate fell below baseline 0.2%. safety-mode will be toggled off gradually to reduce latency. I'll coordinate with CS and product for final customer notes.
jess: notifying affected customers that we've deployed a correctness patch and are restoring normal behavior; follow-up ticket created CS-995. :tada:
evan: great work team — full postmortem scheduled. thanks to everyone for quick coordination. :clap:
